title: Explicit Frobenius mates, outer Weil structures and the unit-counit squares
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme with complementary closed and open immersions $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, and let $X,Z,U,i,j$ be their base changes to $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $F_T=Lg_T^*$ for the geometric-Frobenius automorphisms of $T=X,U,Z$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Fix $\Lambda\in\{A_n,R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ and its specified bounded constructible categories [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Use the canonical adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*$, with open unit $\eta^j$, open counit $\varepsilon$, closed unit $\eta$ and closed counit $\varepsilon^i$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let $b:F_Uj^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*F_X$ and $d:F_Zi^*\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*F_X$ be the canonical pullback-composition comparisons.

The left-adjoint conjugate of $b$ and right-adjoint mate of $d^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] have components
$$\alpha_N=\varepsilon_{F_Xj_!N}\circ j_!(b_{j_!N})\circ j_!F_U(\eta^j_N):j_!F_UN\longrightarrow F_Xj_!N,$$
$$c_M=i_*F_Z(\varepsilon^i_M)\circ i_*(d^{-1}_{i_*M})\circ\eta_{F_Xi_*M}:F_Xi_*M\longrightarrow i_*F_ZM.$$
They are natural isomorphisms. Write $a=\alpha^{-1}:F_Xj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!F_U$. Their normalized mate equations are
$$F_X(\varepsilon_K)=\varepsilon_{F_XK}\circ j_!(b_K)\circ a_{j^*K},\qquad i_*(d_K)\circ c_{i^*K}\circ F_X(\eta_K)=\eta_{F_XK}.$$
The formulas are those of the actual module adjunctions and remain these formulas through finite reduction, completion, rationalization and common-stage scalar extension.

For $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a Weil structure $\theta:F_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], put $A_K=j_!j^*K$, $C_K=i_*i^*K$. The isomorphisms
$$\theta_A=j_!j^*(\theta)\circ j_!(b_K)\circ a_{j^*K},\qquad \theta_C=i_*i^*(\theta)\circ i_*(d_K)\circ c_{i^*K}$$
are their induced Weil structures and satisfy the first two squares
$$\varepsilon_K\circ\theta_A=\theta\circ F_X(\varepsilon_K),\qquad \eta_K\circ\theta=\theta_C\circ F_X(\eta_K).$$
No existence of a localization triangle or equivariance of a connecting map is asserted here, and no triangulated structure on the category of Weil pairs is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the four separate finite, integral/completion, coefficient and localization/descent stage results. Split their conjunctions and place the results in the original eight stage clauses.

For the actual rational and common-stage adjunctions, use the already proved invertibility of their specified open and proper Frobenius exchanges. Define alpha and c by asIso of these actual mates. Mathlib mateEquiv_counit_symm and unit_mateEquiv give the normalized equations after cancellation. Expand mateEquiv to get the explicit three-factor words. Naturality of the open counit and closed unit at theta gives the final two Weil squares; every outer factor is invertible.
